thread:
emily: Hi team — customer Globex (ticket #G-12345) reporting intermittent NXDOMAIN for globexpay.prod.svc.internal from their VPC in us-west-2 after a config migration. ~20% of queries return NXDOMAIN. Repro steps below and minimal logs. Can someone triage?

emily: Repro (from their app node):
```
$ dig @10.0.0.2 globexpay.prod.svc.internal +short
# sometimes returns:
svc-1234.prod.internal.
# sometimes returns nothing -> NXDOMAIN when looked up from app, e.g. dig +norecurse shows 
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NXDOMAIN, id: 5312
```

alex: Thanks — quick checklist: 1) confirm VPC resolver (10.0.0.2) is the one being hit 2) check for duplicate private hosted zones / split-horizon 3) node-local-dns caches in k8s 4) any recent Route53 changes. Do you have the VPC IDs + AWS account IDs? Also which pod/node shows NXDOMAIN?

emily: VPC vpc-0a1b2c3d (acct 987654321000). Both app pods report mixed results across nodes, so seems not a single node issue. Route53 change log shows a hosted zone update ~9m before first report.

maria: Possible overlapped hosted zone in another account or a duplicate private hosted zone accidentally associated to the same name. If there's a private hosted zone with the same name in another account but associated to a resolver rule/forwarder it can cause split-horizon-like behavior. Can you run: 
```
aws route53 list-hosted-zones-by-name --dns-name "globexpay.prod.svc.internal" --profile customer-account
aws route53 get-hosted-zone --id ZZZZZZZZZ
aws ec2 describe-vpc-associations --region us-west-2 --filters Name=hosted-zone-id,Values=ZZZZZZZZ
```

jordan: Also check node-local-dns / kube-proxy caches. If using node-local-dns, try 
```
kubectl -n kube-system get pods -l k8s-app=node-local-dns
kubectl -n kube-system logs ds/node-local-dns -c node-cache | tail -n 100
# trigger cache flush (example): kubectl exec -n kube-system <node-local-pod> -- kill -HUP 1
```

emily: Ran the hosted zone checks. There's a hosted zone in a partner account (acct 111222333444) with the same name but NOT associated to the customer's VPC. However, there is a resolver rule that forwards queries for "prod.svc.internal" to a forwarder in that account. Forwarder appears healthy. Output: 
```
# list-hosted-zones-by-name
{ "HostedZones": [ { "Id": "/hostedzone/Z1ABCDEF", "Name": "globexpay.prod.svc.internal.", "Config": {"PrivateZone": true}, "ResourceRecordSetCount": 12 } ] }
# describe-vpc-associations for Z1ABCDEF -> nothing for vpc-0a1b2c3d
```

alex: Hmm — that suggests a forwarding chain where some queries end up hitting the partner hosted zone and others go to the customer's own hosted zone depending on which resolver/endpoint handled it. Could be timing/routing flap between two resolver endpoints or a resolver rule priority issue. Any recent resolver-rule updates?

emily: There was a resolver rule change ~10m before tickets started: priority change and a new conditional forwarder added. The support-bot also posted an automated deployment notice: 

support-bot: Route53 rule change deployed for customer-forwarders (rollout id r-2026-04-08-09) at 2026-04-08T18:12:03Z.

maria: If forwarders are returning different answer sets (one pointing to the customer's hosted zone and another to partner hosted zone with incomplete records), you will see intermittent NXDOMAIN. Steps: 1) identify which resolver endpoints are in use 2) run dig +trace and dig @<resolver-ip> to see diverging answers 3) confirm hosted zone associations and remove/disable the stale hosted zone or change resolver rule targets.

jordan: For quick repro, run from two different resolver IPs and compare: 
```
# from resolver A (10.0.0.2): dig @10.0.0.2 globexpay.prod.svc.internal +short; dig +trace globexpay.prod.svc.internal
# from resolver B (10.0.1.5): dig @10.0.1.5 globexpay.prod.svc.internal +short
```
If answers differ, capture tcpdump on resolver to see which forwarder it queries.

emily: Did that. Results: resolver A -> returns CNAME -> svc-1234.prod.internal. resolver B -> NXDOMAIN. Traces show resolver B forwarding to partner forwarder which returns NXDOMAIN.

alex: Root cause looks like the partner account hosted zone is shadowing queries for the name in some paths, but it lacks the records or has stale records. Proposed remediation: temporarily disable the new conditional forwarder, or update the partner hosted zone to contain the correct records, or change rule priority so the customer's hosted zone answers first. Please coordinate with partner account or rollback the resolver-rule change.

emily: Escalating to partner ops now. We'll disable the forwarder for the 5-min test window and report back.

emily: Update — disabled forwarder for 5m window, cleared node-local caches, tested: all queries from app nodes now return correct CNAME consistently. Customer confirms degraded behavior stopped.

jordan: Nice. Follow-up actions: 1) create a postmortem entry for the resolver-rule rollout 2) add smoke checks after forwarder changes to detect split answers 3) consider an automated check that flags duplicate private hosted zones across accounts for the same DNS name.

emily: Customer confirmed fix and we're closing ticket #G-12345. Thanks all :tada:
